name: 8.2 Outcomes and the Type I and Type II Errors
_note: Built 2026-08-12. Two reuses (q11-type-i-ii-context, q9-reject-nuanced - both health=ok, never filed) plus nine authored (q25-the-four-outcomes, q26-type-i-error-in-context, q27-type-ii-error-in-context, q28-alpha-beta-power, q29-which-error-costs-more, q30-power-and-beta, q31-error-consequences, q64-both-errors-template, pre-frq-grade-a-type-i-ii-errors) = eleven. Points 9x8 + 8x2 + 12 = 100 (rebalanced from the SPEC's 110 on 2026-08-14 to the every-assignment-is-100 rule). BookSHelf 8.2 is outcomes and the Type I and Type II errors: the four outcomes of a hypothesis test, stating both errors in context, alpha and beta in words, the power of the test 1 - beta, and judging which error carries the heavier consequence. Pre-FRQ is authored-first (no Type I/II FRQ exists anywhere in questions/frq/ - the pre-FRQ defines the scenario and rubric a later FRQ should match): categories State Both Errors in Context (4) / Name the Probabilities (3) / Judge Which Error Costs More (3), dropped category NAME THE PROBABILITIES (a plausible answer states both errors in context and judges their consequences without ever attaching the lettered probabilities).

questions.title: Type I and Type II errors in context - given a scenario with a null hypothesis, identify which outcome corresponds to a Type I error and which corresponds to a Type II error
Reject vs Fail to Reject - nuanced contexts where the p-value is close to the significance level alpha; students must apply the rule rigidly and avoid the accept-the-null misconception
The Four Outcomes - the 2x2 table of decisions crossed with the truth, and which two are the errors
Type I Error in Context - reject a true null, worded about the claim, and the decision it is tied to
Type II Error in Context - fail to reject a false null, worded about the claim, and the decision it is tied to
Alpha, Beta, and Power - what each probability measures, and what the power of the test is
Which Error Costs More - the heavier consequence in a high-stakes scenario, and the reason
Power and Beta - beta = 1 - power, and what the power value means in context
Error Consequences - both errors stated against a flipped null, where swapping H0 and Ha swaps the errors
Both Errors with the Template - Type I and Type II errors stated in context from a stated null

Pre-FRQ Grade a Type I/II Errors - the scenario and grading checklist of the (authored-first) Type I/II errors FRQ, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
